CGI Artist Brings Back the Volkswagen Santana Sedan and Wagon From the Dead, Though Only Virtually
8 photos
Photo: zijie8783 / Instagram
The German automaker Volkswagen has been pretty busy recently in America and Europe, where it launched important models like the 328-hp T-Roc R and, at the Los Angeles Auto Show, presented the Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport family together for the first time alongside the US-exclusive Rabbit Edition for the VW Golf GTI.
All these are fine and dandy, but Volkswagen is falling behind the competition in North America where it offers fewer and fewer models – the electric ID.4 is getting retired soon, and there’s no telling when the all-new ID. Tiguan is coming to the US to replace it. Otherwise, VW sells the all-new Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport plus the Tiguan and Taos as crossover SUVs.
Meanwhile, the passenger car line has just a couple of entries – the compact VW Golf GTI and R hatchbacks of the sporty and hot variety, plus the traditional compact Jetta sedan. Quite obviously, Volkswagen could do better with an additional nameplate or two. Well, here’s a suggestion coming from across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI thanks to a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators.
More precisely, Zijie Yang, a virtual designer better known as ' zijie8783 ' on social media, is actually an Exterior Designer at XPeng, so we'd better pay attention to what he CGIs. On this occasion, the pixel master suggests that Volkswagen should bring back the classic Santana nameplate – and perhaps even sell it in North America.
The original was a series of sedans and station wagon models offered by Volkswagen as an alternative to the Passat nameplate. It was offered since 1981 and also had other names – like the Quantum in North America, Corsar in Mexico, and Carat in Argentina. Production ended the latest in 2022 in China, while Europe hasn’t seen it since 1984 and Latin America since 2006.
Anyway, the CGI expert’s proposal for a revival is tugging at the heartstrings of nostalgia, featuring the styling elements of the 1980s reinterpreted in modern fashion – the dual square headlights are smaller and LED, plus there’s also a dual-tone paint with ‘chrome’ on the bottom half and the grille, plus a squared profile that harkens back to the boxy style of the 1980s.
The wide taillights are now full-width LEDs, and the author crafted both sedan and station wagon versions. The saloon, for example, dressed in silver and blue, is a sportier option with an all-electric powertrain, featuring a black front splitter and a rear diffuser along with black wheels. The station wagon, meanwhile, has pixel-style LED headlights and matching silver wheels along with a silver-and-black treatment. Plus, it’s clearly ICE -powered, as hinted by the dual rear exhaust. Wit more than sixty (60!) new-energy models spanning everything from driverless excavators to cabless loaders and hybrid-electric mining trucks, the next generation of Zoomlion machinery is wowing everyone at bauma 2026.
Closing out a breakout year for the Chinese equipment brand , Zoomlion arrived at bauma China 2026 with more than 60 intelligent, new-energy heavy equipment options spanning eight product categories, highlighting both the company’s manufacturing prowess and establishing it as a leader in what it’s calling, “physical AI.”
And, while the company brought along a few examples of the Z01 and Z03 humanoid robots that are currently building a new equipment asset every six minutes , the real headliner was the cabless Zoomlion excavator robot shown, above.
Zoomlion says its proprietary RobotOps embodied AI operating system built around a vision-language-action (VLA) model that uses a comprehensive suite of sensors to give it “ a 540-degree view ” of the world around it.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Basically marketing-speak for, “ better than just 360 degree camera views ,” the sensors helps the Zoomlion machine correctly identify objects in a variety of conditions, determining their positions, orientations, and dimensions, then using the company’s Zbrain platform to translate that information into physical machine movements – and those movements are “just” being calculated for the excavator.
That 540-degree 3D vision system gives the autonomous excavator a much more complete picture of its surroundings, using multiple sensors to identify obstacles, understand distances, and navigate a constantly changing worksite. ZOOMLION
The company says its intelligent Zbrain platform has been trained on millions of hours of operational data and tens of thousands of real-world scenarios, and allows Zoomlion’s autonomous machines to interpret natural-language job instructions, autonomously deconstructing complex tasks into simple step-by-step workflows before scanning the surrounding terrain, classifying the materials, and determining the right digging and gripping paths to deliver fully automate excavation, loading, slope dressing , brick paving, or material handling.
Free tour guides, too
Zoomlion Z01 robot guide.
The bipedal humanoid Z01 robots will be at the show to guide visitors through the sprawling Zoomlion display, and will reportedly be using facial and gesture recognition to identify and remember individuals, while executing force-compliant motion planning and real-time obstacle avoidance to perform interactive gestures such as fist bumps and waves.
You can check out some photos of Zoomlion’s roboticized and electrified equipment display, below, then let us know what you think about someone else ‘s claims about their AI and robotic sleadership status in the comments.
Zoomlion at bauma 2026

How About a Widebody New-Gen BMW 3 Series (G50)?
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project
There is an entirely new 3 Series in BMW’s portfolio, and due to the Neue Klasse design, it is one of the most controversial ever.
Usually, petrolheads either love it or hate it, as there is no in between, and it has been criticized countless times. But the company poured a huge amount of money into its development, so it wasn’t going to retire it early. Thus, production recently commenced at the Dingolfing factory in Germany for the regular model, whereas its long wheelbase variant comes to life in China.
BMW’s new-gen 3 Series has been discussed numerous times, just like other Neue Klasse models, so this story isn’t about reminding you that the exterior design is on the controversial side of things, nor to put the spotlight on the minimalist interior, which is quite quirky to be honest. Instead, this story is about a tuned example. Actually, make that a virtually tuned one, because the car you see in the gallery does not exist.
Not yet, anyway, because we reckon most big tuners out there, as well as a few small ones, are preparing all kinds of upgrades for the G50 as we speak. In this case, the CGI project was signed by @ildar_project and shared on social media a few days ago, featuring the yellow daytime running lights that are available (on the M350 xDrive), and a very aggressive makeover on the outside that makes it look a lot more muscular.
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project In addition to the fender flares, this particular ride has skits on the lower parts of the body, new trim on the front fenders, and an entirely new hood. The kidney grille has been virtually altered to the point where it somewhat reminds us of the demised i8. The front and rear bumpers feature plenty of changes, too. A sportier ducktail spoiler sits on the trunk lid, and the diffuser has a pair of extra brake lights integrated into it.
Due to the black finish, this BMW M350 xDrive does not look controversial at all, though let’s not forget that this color tends to hide quirky designs like a champ. The wheels are definitely not bad. They are concave, have a Y-spoke pattern, a silver finish, and are a lot bigger than the OEM ones. A look inside is not a thing, because this digital illustration set is all about the exterior of the car.
Before inviting you to reveal your opinion on this virtually-tuned machine, we will remind you that the new BMW M350 xDrive has 437 hp (352 kW /443 ps) and 428 lb-ft (580 Nm) of torque to play with. The familiar twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter straight-six enables 0-60 mph (97 kph) in 4.1 seconds, and that makes it just as fast as the outgoing M3 in its most basic version. So, is this thing a yay or a nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ильдар (@ildar_project)

Moving millions of tons of coal, sugar, and other bulk cargo is serious business, and decarbonizing that business presents a number of unique problems – but if the new BRF Froan bulk carrier proves anything, it’s that battery size isn’t one of them. The new electric cargo ship is packing an impossibly huge, 23,500 kWh battery.
Fitted with the equivalent of nearly 300 long-range electric car batteries, 130 meter (426 ft.) BRF Froam built by SOHO Marine Heavy Industry for Norwegian shipping firm Berge Rederi Future (BRF) will use the ship to haul up to 13,250 deadweight tonnes (DWT) across the 230 nautical miles (or about 265, as the crow flies) between the ports at Brønnøy and Elnesvågen without burning a drop of diesel .
“It’s going to run back and forth, back and forth, just like a ferry,” explains Oivind Berge, co-owner of Berge Rederi Future, in a TradeWinds interview . He added that the round trip takes around 24 hours, with charging facilities installed at the loading and discharge ports. “Then we can go back and forth continuously.”
The 130M vessel BRF Froan left the shipyard at Jiangsu SOHO Marine Heavy Industry, in China last week, and is currently en route to Norway where it is set to begin shipping huge chunks of marble early next year.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
About the stovepipes
BRF Froan; Berge Rederi.
The ship’s massive battery sends electrons to a 6,000 kW (about 8,000 hp) electric motors that turn the propellers. How that works is obvious – what might be less obvious is what those big stovepipe deals at the back of the BRF Froan are.
Those are called rotor, or rotary sails, and they one-up the old-school version by using something call the Magnus effect to produce forward thrust . Basically, as the tall cylinders spin, the wind flowing around them creates a pressure difference that generates lift perpendicular to the wind. That lift produces forward thrust, helping push the ship along and reducing the amount of electricity it needs to draw from its batteries once under way.
The company estimates the two rotary sails will save about 339 kW per trip , while the switch to battery power will save another 10,000 tons of harmful carbon emissions and 220 tons of nitrous oxides each year.
Interesting Engineering is reporting the total cost of the project at approximately USD 52 million (NOK 500 million). A second vessel, named BRF Frøya, is already under construction in China and is scheduled for delivery in 2027.
SOURCE | IMAGES : BRF, via Naval Porto Estaleiro .

Timberline Is a Gorgeous Gooseneck Tiny Home With Two Bedrooms, Two Skylights, and a Huge Kitchen
19 photos
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes
Tiny houses are often praised for the way they maximize the use of space through efficient layouts, multifunctional furniture, and other clever design tricks. Gooseneck tiny houses in particular are loved by many because they typically offer more space and comfort than traditional tiny homes on wheels while still remaining highly mobile.
Though they often come with a higher upfront cost than standard bumper-pull tiny homes on wheels, gooseneck models also offer a larger footprint, improved weight distribution, and towing stability. Because they allow for more generous floor plans and can fit more creature comforts, they are preferred by those who want to make as few compromises as possible when moving into a mobile tiny home.
The Timberline by Summit Tiny Homes is a good example of what makes this type of dwelling so appealing. This is a custom-built, two-bedroom tiny house that would suit both couples and families. It features a spacious interior with distinct areas for lounging, cooking, and sleeping, and combines rustic charm with modern amenities. Two skylights, gorgeous live-edge countertops, full-size appliances, and a bathtub are just some of the features that make it stand out from the crowd.
Based in Vernon, British Columbia, Summit Tiny Homes has been part of the tiny living movement since 2017. The company has recently rebranded as Summit Building Co., a move meant to better reflect its expansion beyond tiny homes into custom modular homes, modern cabins, backyard dwellings (ADUs), and bespoke builds, but its focus is still on creating homes that make small-space living a pleasant experience.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes Built on a triple-axle gooseneck trailer, the Timberline measures 42 feet (12.8 meters) in length and 8.6 feet (2.6 meters) in width. Clad in a combination of natural cedar shake shingles and vertical board-and-batten siding, finished in a deep reddish-brown shade, its exterior exudes a rustic vibe that fits perfectly in any natural setting.
The home is topped by a dark, low-profile metal roof, and black-framed windows with reflective glass adorn its facades. Together, these elements give the tiny house a cabin-inspired appearance that feels both traditional and modern.
Characterized by a clutter-free ambiance, the interior is arranged around everyday comfort, ease of movement, and practicality. The layout includes a large U-shaped kitchen, a central living area, a modern bathroom, and two separate sleeping spaces. The raised gooseneck section above the towing vehicle creates an upper zone with ample headroom, perfect for a more comfortable bedroom compared to a traditional loft.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes Accessed via a few wooden stairs, this gooseneck sleeping space is completely private and feels like a proper bedroom. It fits a queen-size bed and a bedside table, as well as a large wardrobe, while two large windows behind and in front of the bed let ample sunlight in.
The second bedroom is located above the kitchen and is accessed by a built-in staircase with integrated storage cabinets. It’s a traditional low-ceiling loft, but offers a comfortable sleeping space that doesn’t take valuable floor space. It fits a queen mattress and is also quite luminous thanks to side windows and a skylight.
Lying under a ceiling with exposed beams, the kitchen is one of the home's standout features. It has a generous U-shaped configuration that provides plenty of room for meal preparation and storage and a charming homestead aesthetic. It features deep forest-green cabinetry complemented by brass hardware, handcrafted live-edge countertops, and a tiled backsplash.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes The countertop extends into a breakfast bar, providing a nice space for casual meals. For modern functionality, the builder equipped the kitchen with a four-burner propane range, an oven, a microwave, a full-size fridge with freezer, and a large sink. A washer/dryer is neatly integrated under the staircase, adding another layer of convenience for full-time living.
The central living room is not very large, but offers a comfortable place to unwind. An L-shaped sectional sofa placed in front of the glass door and a propane fireplace create a cozy atmosphere. As in most tiny houses, the kitchen and living area are connected in a way that encourages easy movement.
Finally, the bathroom inside the Timberline is surprisingly modern and spacious for a tiny house . Instead of a simple shower stall, it has a bathtub and a tiled shower surround, offering a more luxurious experience. The room also includes a vanity with a cute bowl sink, a toilet, and rustic wooden shelves.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes Another thing that makes this home suitable for full-time living is the abundance of storage solutions. Apart from the storage staircase, the kitchen cabinets, and the wardrobe in the main bedroom, there is also a dedicated storage platform above the bathroom, providing plenty of space for personal belongings.
In terms of styling, the interior combines rich wood ceilings, white shiplap walls, and natural timber accents, creating the warm, calming ambiance of a cozy cabin.
Designed to provide year-round comfort, the Timberline features ZIP System R-sheathing, spray-foam insulation, and triple-glazed windows, which help with thermal bridging. A ductless mini-split system provides heating and air conditioning.
The Timberline is a pre-owned tiny house on wheels that’s now waiting for its next owner. The asking price is CAD $225,000 (around USD$157,900).

He Bought a Tesla Cybertruck for $82,735, Sold It for $94,500 a Year Later
25 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
The pre-owned Tesla Cybertruck market cooled down for a while, only to see prices go through the roof after Elon Musk announced the automaker is winding down production. The original owner of this electric pickup truck bought it last year for $82,735, drove nearly 11,000 miles, and just sold it for nearly $22,000 over sticker.
There was a time when Tesla Cybertrucks flooded the used car market with mind-blowing prices as early owners were trying to cash in. In early 2024, just months after deliveries had started, a Porsche dealership in Orlando paid $244,000 to buy a Cybertruck. Just days later, they relisted it in early March for $289,999 .
The first Cybertruck to hit a public enthusiast auction on Cars & Bids drew 510 comments and stalled at a high bid of $158,000, failing to meet the seller's reserve. From that moment on, Tesla Cybertrucks sold for anything up to $190,000, adding more drama every time and making Tesla executives raise their eyebrows in shock.
We were living in crazy times when the used car market artificially inflated the value of the Cybertruck price even by double, despite Tesla's resale clause that barred owners from selling their trucks during the first year of ownership.
Photo: Cars and Bids As far as we know, a single owner, who had listed his Cybertruck "basically everywhere," had his Tesla orders cancelled as a penalty, was blacklisted and banned from purchasing other Tesla products again. With only the Model 3 and Model Y in the lineup, there isn't really much left to buy, though.
It was by no means a lesson to others who listed their Cybertrucks on online auction platforms to get more than they paid for them. At some point, the market cooled down. In the meantime, Tesla’s inventory had gone out of control, as the automaker parked a gazillion vehicles in shopping mall parking lots or at airports without being able to sell at the pace of production.
The owner of this Cybertruck says he purchased it on November 26, 2025, which means he has just completed the first year of ownership, which means he would by no means be subject to any penalty from Tesla.
However, the automaker has so much on its mind right now that it couldn’t care less about Cybertruck owners selling their Cybertrucks. They have discontinued the model anyway, to reallocate factory space, engineering resources, and resources toward scaling its autonomous Cybercab robotaxi, and are well aware that it can no longer (actually, never could) control the used car market.
Photo: Cars and Bids Now it looks like the market is shifting again because the owner of this 2026 Tesla Cybertruck just sold it for more than he paid for it last year. His electric truck is finished in the usual stainless steel with a Star Wars-inspired partial gray vinyl wrap on the front and tailgate, over a black interior, and rides on 20-inch wheels.
The panoramic glass roof shelters a cabin with heated and ventilated seats and a 15-speaker sound system, typical of the Premium trim. The odometer reads 10,765 miles (17,325 kilometers). The truck stands on Adaptive air suspension, four-wheel steer-by-wire, and Full Self-Driving Capability (FSD), permanently attached to this vehicle and will transfer to the new owner at no extra cost, according to the original owner.
The model rolled off the production line with a dual-motor powertrain, producing 600 horsepower (608 metric horsepower) and 525 pound-feet (712 Newton meters) of torque. That is enough to make it accelerate from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.1 seconds and run the quarter mile in an estimated 12.7 seconds on its way to a top speed of 112 mph (180 kph).
The truck features the 123-kWh battery pack, which stores enough energy for a drive of up to 325 miles (523 kilometers) when it rides on the 20-inch wheels with all-season tires, before it needs to be plugged in again.
Photo: Cars and Bids The owner reports a tire fix at 9,278 miles (14,931 kilometers) earlier this year, and he has already performed a tire rotation, as recommended by the manufacturer. But why did he sell so soon? The owner jumped into the comments section to explain that he has a 2027 Model Y Premium on the way.
He went for the Model Y because he wanted "s omething a little smaller and more practical for daily use. " He bought the Cybertruck without actually needing a Cybertruck. From now on, he will do grocery shopping and road trips with the Model Y.
The EV sold with a clean Carfax report with no accidents or mileage discrepancies. For $94,500, the buyer is taking home two keys, the owner’s manuals, a windshield sunshade, the rear bed mat, adjustable hold-downs and bungee cords, along with the running boards, which are not installed.
Well, they could have bought a far cheaper Cybertruck from a dealership. Dealers sell them between $60,000 and $95,000. Recently, it has become America's fastest selling used pickup truck .

Volkswagen opened orders for the new ID. Buzz Beach in the UK , an electric van built for camping and overnight stays, with a fold-out mattress and more. It’s not exactly cheap, though, starting at over $70,000.
Meet the Volkswagen ID. Buzz Beach
Volkswagen’s original microbus became a cultural icon thanks to its open, customizable interior, making it perfect for large families, road trips, camping, and, of course, music festivals.
The ID. Buzz brings the classic Type 2 microbus into the electric era with a retro-new style, modern tech, and a flexible, spacious cabin.
Building on its reputation as a symbol of freedom and adventure, Volkswagen is adding a new member to the electric people mover lineup.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The new ID. Buzz Beach “brings adventure into the electric age,” Volkswagen said after introducing the new variant on Thursday. Designed for camping, longer road trips, and overnight stays, the electric van will be available in 5-, 6-, and 7-seat configurations.
Volkswagen said it sleeps two comfortably with a removable bed frame and a custom-fitting folding mattress.
Volkswagen ID. Buzz Beach fold-out mattress (Source: VW UK)
The mattress is a decent size at about 6.5 feet long by 4 feet wide (2.0m x 1.2m), roughly the size of an average small double bed.
In the 5-seat configuration, the bed frame tucks away in the trunk, while in the 6- and 7-seat layouts, it’s stored vertically behind the third row of seats.
For camping and other longer stays, Volkswagen added a new Overnight mode that uses the vehicle’s battery to provide up to 48 hours of continuous, off-grid climate control. The new mode can be accessed on the center touchscreen.
It also includes blackout curtains throughout the cabin and ventilation grilles on the front side windows.
The ID. Buzz Beach offers vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities. A 230V power socket adaptor comes standard, letting you power an e-bike, charge a smartphone, run camping equipment, or power other external electronic devices. A camping connector is available as an added option.
To top it off, Volkswagen added a hidden foldable table and chairs set that can be tucked away without taking up internal space.
Volkswagen opened orders for the new ID. Buzz Beach in the UK this week, starting at £53,955 (excluding VAT), or about $71,000. Including VAT and OTR costs, it starts at £65,837, or roughly $86,500.
Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles is offering a few financing deals to get you started, with prices from £555 ($726) a month, including a £6,500 ($8,500) deposit.

ID. Buzz Beach LWB 286 PS 86 kWh Pro Electric 1-Speed Automatic RWD 7-seater | £54,395 ($71,200) | £66,365 ($86,900)
Volkswagen ID. Buzz Beach prices by trim in the UK
What about those in the US? Will Volkswagen bring the electric camper to the States?
Top comment by ModernMarvalFan
Liked by 9 people
Nice product at the wrong price. If VW can't lower the price because of the cost, then it has a lot more work to do to compete in this market.
View all comments
VW introduced the 2027 ID. Buzz with a new Tourer model that was essentially the same as the Beach variant in the UK, with a fold-out mattress, Overnight mode, blackout curtains, and a table and chairs set.
However, VW told its US dealers in September that it would be delaying the ID. Buzz’s return until the 2028 model year.
The 2025 Volkswagen ID. Buzz started at about $60,000 in the US, which is one of the biggest reasons it failed to catch on with buyers. The original VW microbus was an affordable people mover.
A custom camper variant would likely cost more than $70,000. Would you pay $70,000 or more for Volkswagen’s electric camper van?

source_document.body:
The most shocking thing about the recent investors day presentation held by Expeditors International is that it was taking place at all.
Daniel Wall, the president and CEO of the asset-light freight forwarder–among several other services–conceded at the start of the November 18 investors day event that “if you know me well, you know I probably came here kicking and screaming a little bit.”
Expeditors (NYSE: EXPD) does not have an earnings call with analysts after it releases its quarterly earnings. Wall said the investors day was the first Expeditors had held in 11 years.
Unlike other company investor days, which are usually closed-door and open just to analysts who follow the company, Expeditors’ was broadcast and anybody could have signed up for it if they were aware of its existence.
“We have to engage better with the investment community,” Wall said, according to a transcript of the event. “And today is an attempt to do that. We’re going to give you some insights into some things that we don’t normally share.”
CFO with the big reveal
Most of the revelations about Expeditors’ business that had not been released previously came from Dave Hackett, the company’s CFO. He spoke of “two things that we’ve never disclosed.”
The first, which he described as “a little bit tactical but strategic,” was the role of Expeditor’s business tied to technology and by extension, AI.
Hackett revealed that 35% of Expeditors’ gross revenue is coming from its technology vertical. That is by far the largest; healthcare is second at 14%.
The pre-AI comparison, Hackett said, is that technology was about 28% of the company’s gross revenue in 2019.
“So is a lot of that AI?” Hackett said. “Yes. Is AI driving our results? Absolutely.”
Expeditors, Hackett said, is “heavily concentrated in the capex supercycle of the century. So that is a good thing and we’re performing very well.”
Business with hyperscalers was cited by Expeditors in its most recent quarterly earnings as a key driver of profitability.
The other verticals and their share of gross revenue disclosed by Hackett were retail, 13%; automotive, 12%; industrial, 6%; and aviation, 4%, leaving 14% to 15% for all other markets.
What’s in the customs brokerage operations?
The second big numerical reveal, which Hackett referred to as “more strategic,” was the breakdown in revenues for its customs brokerage segment.
Expeditors’ quarterly earnings report separate revenue figures for airfreight services, ocean freight and ocean services, and customs brokerage and other services. In the most recent quarterly earnings, airfreight was approximately 37.6% of revenues, ocean was about 26.8% with customs brokerage the balance at a little over 35%.
Hackett said that customs brokerage number can approach 50%, depending on the performance of the other two segments.
But within that segment, Hackett said, “A lot of investors and analysts think it’s all customs brokerage. It is not.”
The chart revealed by Hackett showed that customs brokerage revenues were 47% of the segment that carries that name in the quarterly earnings.
Its Transcon operations, which services the over-the-ground industry, is 37% of the segments’ revenue. In its most recent 10-K filing, Expeditors said Transcon “consists of intra-continental ground transportation, including time-definite less-than-truck and full-truck solutions.”
The remaining 16% of the segment is from warehousing & distribution. That Expeditors’ 10-K said its warehousing operations offer services such as inventory management and “are generally offered globally in multi-client facilities so that customers may benefit from cost savings related to shared space, labor, equipment, and other efficiencies.”
Hackett added he would not discuss the profitability of the sectors. There also was not a timeframe disclosed for those figures.
(An expanded area for Expeditors was recently announced: space travel. )
TD Securities raises its rating
The transportation research team at TD Securities led by Jason Seidl liked what they heard enough that they upgraded their rating to Hold from Sell within days after the investors meeting.
In its report, TD Securities noted that the discussion by Expeditors’ management about the use of AI in the company differed from what is heard from the leaders of C.H. Robinson (NASDAQ: CHRW). While the two companies are not head-to-head competitors in many businesses, they both are asset-light entities whose value proposition is to take responsibility for moving freight from point A to point B away from their customers and shifting it on to their own expert staff.
C.H. Robinson has seen a sharp reduction in headcount as it promotes its use of lean AI. But as TD Securities noted, the message from Expeditors was different.
“EXPD spent a significant portion of the day highlighting their employees, tenure and retention,” the TD report said. “EXPD does not plan to roll out a significant automation effort that will drive SG&A leverage but instead take a methodical approach to driving productivity and wallet share gains.”
It was noted by at least one analyst following the $EXPD investors day call that it is pushing AI as an efficiency tool. But unlike $CHRW , which had an average 3Q payroll about 10% less than a year ago, Expeditors isn't slashing bodies. pic.twitter.com/WAYt3VQNvb — John Kingston (@JohnHKingston) November 27, 2026
In line with that, Courtney Hawkins, the company’s CIO, said the “most important” slide she was showing to the audience was that Expeditors has had an 8.9% increase in shipments and a less than 1% drop in headcount. (The time frame for that point of comparison was not made clear).
By contrast, C.H. Robinson total headcount between the third quarter of 2025 and 2026 was down more than 10%.
At Bank of America Merrill Lynch, the team led by Ken Hoexter (who was on the investors’ day call) did not increase its rating on Expeditors, which already was at a Buy. But it increased its price target to $234 from $230.
Expeditors’ stock closed Friday at $199.46. It had closed November 18 at $188.88 and appears to have gotten some boost from the investors call, though given volatility in the overall market it can be challenging to cite the meeting as the cause of the increase.
The bank’s report also cited some of the data behind its improved price target. “Expeditors set a target for 5% to 7% long-term organic growth, and 12% to 15% EPS growth,” Bank of America Merrill Lynch said. “It raised its operating margin floor target (operating efficiency) to 32.5% from 30%.
Possible M&A reentry
Besides not holding earnings calls with analysts or investor days, one thing Expeditors also hasn’t done in a long time is make an acquisition.
Wall said Expeditors had not made a major acquisition since it entered the ocean business in 1986 with the acquisition of Pac Bridge. In recounting that, Wall noted he was a senior in high school that year.
But Hackett opened the door to that strategy changing.
In response to an analyst’s question, Hackett said an acquisition would need to be one that did not impact Expeditors’ culture, which the management team discussed at length earlier in the presentation.
But he added Expeditors had not been active in making acquisitions even when it was the type of deal that might not impact culture.
“We’re just going to be more active in the market to seize opportunities of value when they come up and provide competitive advantage,” Hackett said. But he added “I don’t want to go much further than that.”
Let’s do this again sometime
Toward the end of the call, Ravi Shanker of Morgan Stanley thanked the Expeditors’ management, adding that “I hope the message you guys are getting from us is we really like hearing from you, and we would like to hear from you more often.”
Shanker then got specific: any plans to add conference calls with analysts each quarter?
“We’re not committed yet,” Hackett said. “We’re evolving our investor relations strategy. This is part of that.”
To which Wall, who said earlier in the call that it was mostly Hackett who pushed the idea of the meeting, added, “Yes, this has been really uncomfortable.”

1964 Studebaker Wagonaire Junkyard Find Is a Rare Classic With an Innovative Feature
12 photos
Photo: Steve Magnante/YouTube
In 1961, Studebaker hired industrial designer Brooks Stevens to restyle the Hawk series and the Lark on a limited budget. He was also tasked with expanding the company's limited model range, which resulted in the Wagonaire hitting showrooms for the 1963 model year.
The Wagonaire was based on the Lark compact, which was already available as a station wagon. However, the Wagoinare was brand-new above the beltline, with the roofline inspired by Stevens' 1959 Scimitar concept. More importantly, it had a retractable panel over the cargo bay, a feature that wasn't available on any other wagon at the time.
Brooks developed the partially retractable roof in 1962 on a prototype called Skyview. But with Studebaker unable to develop a brand-new car, Stevens opted to redesign it for the Lark-based Wagonaire. The panel retracted into the forward section of the roof, where it locked into position. The headliner was lowered to provide clearance for the roof panel and the tracks.
The sliding roof enabled the Wagonaire to haul items that were too tall to fit inside a regular wagon trunk. Studebaker bragged that it could transport standard-size refrigerators in an upright position but also advertised the vehicle as an open-air convertible.
Print ads include photos of people stargazing through a telescope from the open rear bay or children playing with balloons while sitting in the trunk. But the Wagonaire didn't catch on as a leisure vehicle. And needless to say, the ability to haul tall items didn't make it particularly popular either.
Built from 1963 until 1966, the Wagonaire moved just under 20,000 units. Nearly 12,000 of these cars were sold in the first year, with an additional 5,163 delivered in 1964. About 12,000 are said to have been sold with the sliding roof feature (Studebaker also offered a regular roof version in all years except 1965).
Unfortunately, most of these grocery-getters are no longer around. While some have been restored and are still on the road, most are rotting away in junkyards and barns. Classic car enthusiasts recently found a 1964 example in a junkyard in Halifax, Massachusetts. It's one of those vehicles that was built before Studebaker closed its South Bend plant, and, yes, it has the sliding roof.
Studebaker sold 5,163 units during the 1964 model year. That number isn't small enough to call this wagon rare, but the original engine that's still under the hood suggests that it's actually pretty scarce. The mill in question is an inline-six. Studebaker offered both straight-six and V8 powerplants that year, and the former found its way into only a third of all the cars.
The mill is a 194-cubic-inch (3.2-liter) six-cylinder and was favored by 1,784 customers. This Wagonaire is most likely a base Commander model, which means it's one of 1,206 units made, according to existing data. The Challenger version would be much rarer, with only 453 units made.
The sliding roof panel is still in place, which is pretty cool, but the Studebaker is in a sorry state. It's quite obvious that it's been sitting for decades, and it has developed severe rust issues. Is it worth rescuing? Well, let's say that it wouldn't make sense financially since these wagons are far from valuable today.
However, with most of these cars having already morphed into rust buckets, examples that are still in one piece should be rescued in order to keep the Wagonaire legacy alive. Hopefully, someone will want to make it their labor of love, and we'll see it back on the road someday.

Mobile
JetKVM Mini-Screen 1
We have been testing the JetKVM Mini W (and the wired Mini) for some time, and it is time for a review. The Mini W’s “W” stands for wireless, since it connects to the network wirelessly. Another neat part about this is the price. At $42 each, these are inexpensive for what they offer. Despite being inexpensive, this did not feel “cheap.” We will get into why in the review along with some things we would want to change, and some bits that were executed very well.
JetKVM Mini W Hardware
The box itself is roughly 1.7″ x 1.7″ x 0.9″, so it is really small. If you need to put a KVM in a bag, this is great. Also, the chassis is mostly aluminum, so it is small but feels premium, whereas you almost expect something small and inexpensive to be plastic and cheap.
JetKVM Mini-Top Angled 1
The screen on this little box is useful and is a big plus versus something like the GL.iNet Comet GL-RM1 . The screen shows us a PIN for setup and can show you the IP address of the KVM. A small bummer is that it is not a touchscreen, so you navigate the menus with two side buttons.
JetKVM Mini-Screen 2
Another challenge is internal storage for mounting ISOs and such. Here, you get a TF card slot, so you can add a microSD card for local storage ( Amazon Affiliate ). That adds about 50% of the unit’s cost, so we understand why JetKVM left it out, but having Ubuntu, Proxmox VE, and our custom AgentSTH ISOs loaded on it is super useful.
JetKVM Mini-Side 3
On the side, we get to buttons to navigate the menus.
JetKVM Mini-Side 4
Then comes the most important side with two USB Type-C ports and an HDMI port. We have an early unit that came from JetKVM, but clearly these need to be labeled. On the website, the ports have labels.
JetKVM Mini-Front 1
The left Type-C port (as shown below) is for the connection to the managed system. The center Type-C port is for power input.
JetKVM Mini-USB Type-C Ports 1
We got two Type-A to Type-C cables to provide both data and power connections for the unit.
JetKVM Mini-USB Type-C to USB Type-A Cables 1
Finally, the HDMI port is for HDMI input from the managed system.
JetKVM Mini-HDMI Port 1
We got a little HDMI cable as well.
JetKVM Mini-HDMI to HDMI Cable 1
Next, let us get to the software setup.
JetKVM Software Setup
This is one of the more interesting ones. Since you do not have a wired network port, you cannot get a DHCP address. Instead, JetKVM’s website uses a local phone or PC/ Mac to pair with the device.
JetKVM Mini W Website to Pair the Device
Then, you can set up the WiFi and find the IP address for the unit.
JetKVM Mini W Paired and Ready
Once that is complete, you can navigate to the IP address and finish setup.
JetKVM Mini W Setup 1
There are a few steps you can complete, but one interesting one is that you can use a password or passwordless login.
JetKVM Mini W Local Authentication
Overall, the setup process was easy once you realize you need to pair the unit to set it up.
Next, let us get to the interface.

The Only Numbers-Matching 1970 Plymouth Sport Fury GT 440 Six-Barrel Took 27 Years To Restore
39 photos
Photo: Facebook/Brad Miles
By 1970, Detroit's horsepower fever was already colliding with steep insurance rates and shifting buyer tastes, yet Chrysler refused to blink. While rivals abandoned full-size performance, Plymouth bolted its fiercest three-twos (that’s triple two-barrels) big-block straight into a two-door C-body cruiser. The result was the 1970 Plymouth Sport Fury GT 440 Six-Barrel, an improbably sleek fuselage titan with quarter panels bigger than a starter apartment and cutthroat Mopar brawn hidden beneath its hood.
Jim Campisano, the automotive sleuth from Muscle Car Campy , spotlighted one of these unicorns at the Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals. Owned by Bill Hanzlik of Shorewood, Minnesota, the Burnt Orange hardtop sits atop the full-size Mopar hierarchy. Plymouth built 1,306 US-market Sport Fury GTs for 1970, equipping just 61 with the 440+6.
History has been very cruel to that limited batch of full-size brawlers. Fifty of them are mere memories at best, and among the eleven surviving examples, this is the sole numbers-matching car. Royalty at its finest.
The centerpiece rests under that sprawling hood: the E87 440-cubic-inch V8 fed by three two-barrel Holley carburetors. Crucially, Plymouth did not detune this 7.2-liter powerhouse for C-body duty. It matched the GTX, Road Runner, and 'Cuda spec for spec, delivering 390 horsepower at 4,700 rpm and 490 lb-ft of torque at 3,200 rpm with a 10.5:1 compression ratio. Every Six-Barrel GT paired this mill with a TorqueFlite automatic and 3.23 gears.
Photo: Facebook/Rocket Restorations Still, raw torque can only bend the laws of physics so far when hauling more than two tons of Detroit steel. When Road Test magazine put a 1970 Sport Fury GT 440+6 through its paces back in the day, the hardtop tipped the scales at 4,216 pounds and crossed the quarter mile in 16.01 seconds at 92.5 mph. The editors dubbed it a suave boulevardier rather than a pure racer with a dietary problem.
This particular example began its journey on September 4, 1969, when it was scheduled for assembly at Chrysler's Newark, Delaware plant. It was originally ordered by the owner of Doug Griffith Auto Sales, a Baltimore, Maryland Chrysler-Plymouth dealership, for his personal use, though it sold upon arrival. Carrying $752.50 in options, including $153.45 for the Six-Barrel big-block , over its $3,898 base price, the coupe stickered at $4,650.50 plus $85 destination.
Decades later, that same Maryland-delivered Mopar caught the eye of Bill Hanzlik. Already owning several four-barrel examples, Hanzlik knew how seldom a genuine Six-Barrel Sport Fury GT ever surfaced on the open market. The moment this car popped up for sale in 1999, he immediately claimed it as his own. What followed was a 27-year restoration marathon that finally wrapped up in 2026, outlasting plenty of marriages, as Campisano jokingly remarked.
Photo: YouTube/Muscle Car Campy Restoring an obscure C-body Plymouth is nothing like ordering catalog parts for a Camaro or Chevelle, because reproduction houses virtually ignore these cars. Hanzlik spent years chasing factory-correct hardware, occasionally purchasing entire donor cars just to salvage a single unobtainable item like an intact dash pad. The toughest treasures were the rocker moldings. Across 30 years, Hanzlik saw only four new-old-stock pieces offered, and two now sit on this car.
The tail end posed an equally delicate challenge thanks to its thin aluminum rear bumper finish panel. As Hanzlik remarked, merely looking at that trim piece cross-eyed is enough to dent it, making an undamaged survivor nearly impossible to locate. Visually, though, the payoff is extraordinary. The coupe wears FK3 Burnt Orange Metallic, a Fury-only hue applied to 145 Sport Fury GTs and often confused with FK5 Deep Burnt Orange.
Under fluorescent indoor lighting, the metallic paint shifts toward a warm creamsicle tone before deepening in natural sunlight. It pairs with a Champagne vinyl roof seen on 89 units and a matching Burnt Orange bucket-seat cabin boasting a huge console, floor shifter, and radio-delete dash found on 51 cars. Hideaway headlights, strobe stripes echoed on Rallye wheel caps, hood-mounted turn signals, and Sport Fury side-marker lenses complete the vintage spectacle.
Photo: YouTube/Muscle Car Campy Even that hood tells a story, sharing its stamping with every 1970 Fury, police cars included, while the A01 Light Package added recessed hood blinkers. Beneath it, the restoration obeys strict original-equipment standards rather than over-restored flash.
Every gloss-black finish, date code, component part number, and wiring harness label matches factory specs, down to the embossed trunk molding number, duplicated faithfully from reference photographs captured before disassembly ever began.
Bringing this colossal coupe back to life fell to Rick Kreuziger of Restorations by Rick in Merrillan, Wisconsin, who spent roughly 15 years pacing the job while Hanzlik hunted down prime parts. Detroit built these cruisers as 3- or 4-year throwaways rather than 50-year collectibles, leaving heavy rust along the lower quarter panels.
Photo: YouTube/Muscle Car Campy Because clean full panels simply do not exist, Kreuziger painstakingly hand-massaged and repaired virtually every corner himself.
Interior panels proved just as punishing, since decades of dampness warped the original backing boards beyond straightening. Kreuziger stripped the upholstery, removed the metal inserts, fabricated brand-new boards, and rebuilt each panel to look completely untouched.
Campisano likened seeing a Six-Barrel Sport Fury GT to Halley's Comet landing in your backyard, and after 27 years of relentless dedication, this 1,200-mile-ready grand tourer proves patience still beats rust and time.

Low-Mileage Ferrari 488 Pista Demands Access To Your Bank Account
12 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
Can you believe it’s only been six years since Ferrari pulled the plug on the 488? We (or I in this case) though that it is a lot older, but let’s not forget that assembly commenced back in 2015.
Over the years, the Prancing Horse offered it as a two-door berlinetta (coupe) and with a retractable hard top (Spider), and there have been some special editions, as well, including the 488 Pista Piloti, and the J50. The KC23, P80/C, and SP38 Deborah were one-offs, and the 488 GTB and 488 Spider were joined by the 488 Pista and 488 Pista Spider.
These remain sought-after models, and it’s easy to understand why. After all, they are more track-focused supercars than their mainstream models, and it’s worth noting that the Pista’s design was influenced by the 488 Challenger and the 488 GTE racers. Besides the exterior mods, it also had some changes on the inside, mostly with a weight-saving focus, and also boasted more power.
Ferrari fans know that the 488 Pista was 200 pounds (91 kg) lighter than the 488 GTB, and had 49 hp (50 ps/37 kW) and 74 lb-ft (100 Nm) of torque more. The uprated twin-turbocharged 3.9-liter V8 engine was rated at 710 hp (720 ps/530 kW) and 568 pound-feet (770 Nm) of torque, enabling 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in 2.85 seconds, or almost two-tenths of a second faster than the GTB. From 0-124 mph (0-200 kph), it needed 7.6 seconds, and it hit over 211 mph (340 kph) flat out.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago Pictured in the gallery is a 2020 model year Ferrari 488 Pista , presented in blue, with orange racing stripes running across its length. It sports anthracite wheels with a V-spoke design, has red brake calipers, an orange leather interior with plenty of black details, a flat-bottom steering wheel with red stitching, black pillars, an orange headliner, and the usual gear expected from such a thing.
This is definitely an interesting spec, and while some might argue that it would look best if it were dressed in other colors, others would say that it is simply perfect. Where do you stand on that? Actually, before inviting you to leave your impression on this Ferrari 488 Pista, we also have to tell you that it has in the region of 3,000 miles (~4,800 km) on the clock. Therefore, it hasn’t seen that much action over the years.
The selling dealer, which is known as @motorcarsofchicago on Instagram, offers financing, accepts trade-ins, and is asking for a lot of money for this Ferrari 488 Pista . In fact, at the time of writing, the older Italian supercar was advertised for $1,399,995. Keep in mind that this model tends to fetch between $750,000 and over $1.4 million, depending on the mileage, spec, condition, and other factors. source_document.body:
After becoming the world’s first all-electric 40 ton class articulated haul truck into regular series production earlier this year, the Volvo A40 has finally reached its first customers in the UK – and they wasted no time putting the big BEV to work on one of the nation’s largest, most important infrastructure projects.
More than sixty years after Volvo’s “ Gravel Charlie ” invented the articulated hauler, Volvo CE has delivered four customer A40 Electric articulated haul trucks to BMJV (a joint venture between Bouygues Travaux Publics and J Murphy & Sons) for use on the Lower Thames Crossing, further demonstrating that zero-emission machines are ready to move material at scale at major job sites right now .
“Going electric today is no longer about compromise, it’s about the benefits,” explains Shaun Pidcock, Lower Thames Crossing Programme Director at BMJV. “These remarkable machines show that even the heaviest jobs can be done cleanly, and in a way that is better for those working on or living near our sites.”
The Lower Thames Crossing project is approximately 14.3 miles long, and includes more than 2.5 miles of tunnels criss-crossing beneath the River Thames. Once finished, the project will connect the Kent and Essex meters, and promises to nearly double road capacity across the east side of London while becoming the first major infrastructure program in Britain completed with carbon-neutral construction.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
By using the next generation of construction machinery to make the Lower Thames Crossing Britain’s greenest road today, we are helping the industry set a new standard for tomorrow and make diesel-powered sites a thing of the past. SHAUN PIDDOCK BMJV
Since grid power isn’t available on site, BMJV is using fuel cell generators fueled by British-manufactured green hydrogen to charge the A40s. The generators produce no exhaust emissions and are noticeably quieter than combustion machines, further improving living and working conditions for the humans around the site.
The A40 Electric, itself
Volvo A40 Electric haul trucks; by BMJV.
The “40” in the A40 Electric’s badge refers to the truck’s whopping 40 ton (39 tonne) payload capacity. Once loaded up, the hauler’s 350 kW (about 470 hp) electric motor sends power through a torque-amplifying gear reduction gearbox that, depending on how you do the math, delivers some 200,000 lb-ft of “at the wheel” torque. More than enough twisting force, in other words, to match the performance of diesel and possibly enough to have a measurable impact on the rotational speed of a planet.
That motor draws power from a 540 kWh li-ion battery good for up to six hours of continuous operation, but the hauler’s advanced regenerative braking system usually collects enough energy during operation to make it good for a full day’s shift. And, if there’s a Circle K nearby , operators can plug their A40 Electric into a 350 kW DC fast charger and get their battery from 10% to 90% in about an hour.
And, since today is “ Black Friday ,” I’d be remiss if I didn’t point out that fans of Volvo Construction Equipment, LEGO, or both will want to check out the awesome, totally related sets listed, below:
LEGO Technic Volvo CE sets :
LEGO Technic Volvo FMX Truck & EC230 Electric Excavator
LEGO Technic Volvo L120 Electric Wheel Loader
LEGO Technic Volvo EC500 Hybrid Excavator
LEGO Technic 6×6 Volvo Articulated Hauler
